slots.purpose: Set an expert, calm, luxury tone: the moment of looking closely at a diamond before buying.
slots.shot_brief: A single loose round brilliant diamond held in diamond tweezers above a soft grey grading tray, a jeweller's loupe resting beside it, a folded plain sheet of paper (no visible text) in soft focus. Late-morning window light, crisp sparkle, shallow depth of field. No jeweller, lab or brand logos, packaging or recognisable designs. Never copy GIA or IGI diagrams, master-stone photos or report layouts. No people, or one anonymous cropped hand. No real place. Landscape 3:2 with negative space for a title crop. Licensed photography strongly preferred (stock bought by a human and registered in library-index.csv, or a commissioned shoot).

slots.purpose: Help the reader picture the D-to-Z colour scale and how setting metal changes perceived colour.
slots.shot_brief: Option A (diagram): a simple horizontal band from colourless to faint yellow with the grade groups D-F colourless, G-J near colourless, K-M faint, N-Z very light to light, as own artwork, no photographic master stones. Option B (still life): two similar loose round diamonds, one set in a white-metal prong head and one in a yellow-gold head, side by side to show how metal colour reflects into the stone. Neutral background (soft grey paper, linen or warm stone), soft diffused daylight, true-to-life colour, editorial and uncluttered. No people, or only anonymous cropped hands. No real place. slots.purpose: Show the reader what to look for on a grading report (report number, 4Cs, shape and measurements, origin statement, inscription) without showing a real report.
slots.shot_brief: Generic, fictional mock-up of a diamond grading report built by the team: an invented neutral layout, the word 'SAMPLE' across it, placeholder report number clearly fake (for example 'Report no. 0000000000'), labelled callouts pointing to report number, shape and measurements, colour, clarity, cut (where graded), fluorescence, origin (natural or laboratory-grown) and laser inscription. Optional inset: a stylised girdle with an inscription line. Never a real GIA or IGI report, never a lab name or logo on the document, never a copy of either lab's layout, fonts or security features. Flat, top-down, brand palette.
